- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect risk aversion.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in the next 3–5 periods to avoid overcorrection.  
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., recent prices trending down from peak), model often fails to revert; apply slight downward bias (1–3%) to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before projecting.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
